mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary tightening, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 6-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate sales and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 6-month MA AND HOUST < 6-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above its 5-year average, combined with stable unemployment, signals increased labor supply without commensurate job creation, which compresses wages and reduces consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS > 5-year MA for 6 consecutive months
regime_hint: labor supply expansion without job growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising above its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumption propensity, which depresses demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.
